findings.F1: In coins whose 90-day return is negative, an up-day is given back the next day, and more so the larger it is: the excess 1-day return falls by 0.576 % per unit of the up-day in 20-day standard deviations (t -2.73, 1051 non-overlapping cases). At 3 days the slope is -1.11 % per unit (t -1.86, 353 cases), and at 5 days it disappears (+0.33 %, t 0.29, 183 cases). In coins whose 90-day return is not negative, the same slope is positive: +0.40 % per unit at 1 day (t 2.02, 1146 cases) and +1.25 % at 3 days (t 1.98, 381 cases).
findings.F2: The tested idea's effect sits in the largest up-days of rising coins. With the recorded regime trending, up-days of 1 to 2 usual moves are followed by +1.83 % excess over 5 days (t 2.13, 170 cases), and those above 2 usual moves by +5.53 % (t 2.62, 59 cases). With the regime not trending, the slope on up-days is -0.35 % per unit (t -0.57, 641 cases).
findings.F3: The coin's 90-day direction persists over 5 days only when the coin is calm. In the lowest third of each coin's 20-day volatility, a non-negative 90-day return is followed by +0.90 % excess over 5 days (t 2.39, 505 cases), and a negative one by -0.76 % (t -2.03, 491 cases). In the middle and top thirds, every mean is between -0.47 % and -0.05 % with |t| ≤ 0.93.
findings.F4: The book earns only when it holds large positions, which under vol targeting means calm coins. Held bars in the top quartile of allocation have a next-day excess return of +0.226 % (t 2.40, 2214 bars). The two lowest quartiles have -0.197 % (t -1.74) and -0.173 % (t -1.64).
findings.F5: The book's losses come from a few crashes while it is long. The worst 1 % of position-bars (174 bars, mean allocation 1.14, mean coin move that day -9.55 %) carry 25 % of all its negative position gain. Its worst 2 % of days average -5.19 % against a coin move of -8.49 %, which is consistent with the Calmar of 0.53 failing.
findings.F6: Day-of-week returns look like a pattern but do not stand out from chance. Wednesday's excess 1-day return is negative in all 6 coins (-0.14 % to -0.40 %) and Thursday's is positive in all 6 (+0.11 % to +0.61 %). But averaged across coins per day the t-statistics are only -1.30 and +1.29, Friday's is 2.17, and the Thursday-and-Friday minus Monday-and-Wednesday gap shrinks from +0.18 to +1.76 % before 2022 to -0.13 to +0.63 % after. I propose no idea from it.

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 90-day return is negative, a one-day rise is given back over the next day. The larger that rise in units of its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns, the larger the fall over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A sharp up-day in a coin in a long fall is a reason to go short for the following day rather than to chase it.
ideas.name: downtrend bounces fade overnight

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 20-day standard deviation of daily returns is low against its own past, the direction of its 90-day return continues over the next 5 days. The calmer the coin, the larger the move in that direction.
ideas.consequence: In a calm coin, the sign of its 90-day return is a reason to hold a position its way for the next days, and in a turbulent coin it is no reason at all.
ideas.name: calm coins keep trending
